We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

We have guidance: three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). 2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid). 3) amide coupling (carboxylic acid + amine). So retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide bond to give acid and aniline (or aniline derivative). Then break the α,β-unsaturated acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forms α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. So retro step: cut the C=C and C=O to give aldehyde and malonic acid? The product of Doebner is unsaturated acid attached to aromatic ring (the aryl part). In our target, the unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring via C=C to carbonyl amide. Wait structure: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So we have aryl ring (sulfonyl phenyl) attached to a side chain: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline (with NH2). So the α,β-unsaturated acid is actually the acid before amide formation: /C=C/COOH attached to aromatic ring. Then amide coupling attaches the aniline (c3ccccc3N) to the acid.

Thus retrosynthesis: Step1 (reverse amide coupling): break amide to give α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Step2 (reverse Doebner): break α,β-unsaturated acid to give aromatic aldehyde (aryl-CHO) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Step3 (reverse sulfonamide formation): break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and aniline (the first phenyl ring with NH2). Wait sulfonamide is between the first phenyl (with methyl) and sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. Actually target has NS(=O)(=O) attached to first phenyl (para methyl). So sulfonamide formed from aniline (first phenyl with NH2) and sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl (the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl). So retro step: break N-S bond to give aniline (first phenyl) and sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl (aryl-SO2Cl). So we need three steps: 1) amide disconnection, 2) Doebner disconnection, 3) sulfonamide disconnection.

Now we need to find appropriate template IDs for each transformation. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria to find templates for amide formation (reverse: amide bond cleavage). Functional groups broken: amide (so broken: amide). Formed: carboxylic acid and amine. Let's search.
